learning_outcomes.text: To have knowledge about random variables and probability functions
To have knowledge about discrete and continuous distributions
To have knowledge about statistical analysis methods

syllabus_topics: Introduction to probability
Discrete and continuous random variables
Discrete and continuous distributions
Statistical estimation
Statistical hypothesis testing
Regression and Variance analysis
Introduction to probability, sample space and event, compound event, probability axioms
Conditional probability, tree diagrams, total probability formula, Bayes' theorem, independence
Distribution and density functions of continuous and discrete random variables, mean and standard deviation values
Moment concept, relationship between moments, Chebyshev's inequality
Bivariate (joint) discrete and continuous random variables
Conditional probability distributions, example problems
Concepts of covariance, correlation and correlation coefficient
Problem solving
Discrete distributions: Bernoulli, binomial, negative binomial, geometric, Poisson and hypergeometric
Continuous distributions: uniform, exponential, normal distributions
Sampling, statistical estimation, confidence interval of estimation
Hypothesis tests, power of the test, independence test
Regression analysis: linear regression, least squares method, multiple regression
Variance analysis
assessment_rules: Midterm and final exam dates are not specified in the 14-week course schedule. Midterm and final exam dates are held on the dates specified in the academic calendar by the decision of our University Senate.
bibliography: Stark, H., Woods J. W., Probability and Random Processes with Applications to Signal Processing, Third edition, Prentice Hall, 2002
Papoulis A., Pillai S.U., Probability, Random Variables and Stochastic Processes, Fourth edition, McGraw Hill, 2002.
